ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the horizontal axis is labeled Re G(s), and the vertical axis is labeled Im G(s). The Nyquist curve contains a large outer elliptical closed loop, as well as two small loops near the negative real-axis side. The position of -1 is marked on the real axis, and the positions of approximately -0.8 and -0.4 are marked with dashed lines; the two small loops are roughly located near -0.8 to 0. The curve arrows show that the large outer loop travels clockwise; the left small loop also travels clockwise; the right small loop does not enclose the -0.5 point. Reasoning: The closed-loop characteristic equation is 1 + K G(s) = 0, therefore on the Nyquist plot of G(s), the critical point -1/K should be examined. Given K = 2, the critical point is -1/2 = -0.5. Judging from the scale in the figure, -0.5 is between -0.8 and -0.4. This point is enclosed once by the large outer loop, and also enclosed once by the left small loop, but is not enclosed by the right small loop. According to the arrows, these two relevant encirclements are both clockwise encirclements, therefore the net number of clockwise encirclements is 2. The problem states that G(s) has no poles in the closed right half-plane, so P = 0. Under the Nyquist criterion, the number of closed-loop poles in the closed right half-plane equals this net number of clockwise encirclements, namely 2.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify the real and imaginary axes and the plotted loops of G(s). From the text K=2, compute the critical point on the G(s) plot as -1/K = -0.5. Using the image scale, locate -0.5 between the marked -0.8 and -0.4 positions. Count the loops enclosing this point: the large outer loop encloses it once, and the left small loop encloses it once; the right small loop does not. Follow the arrows to confirm both relevant encirclements are clockwise. Since G(s) has no closed-RHP poles, P=0, so the number of closed-loop poles in the closed RHP is the net clockwise encirclement count, 2.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中横轴标为 Re G(s)，纵轴标为 Im G(s)。Nyquist 曲线包含一个大的外椭圆形闭合回路，以及靠近负实轴一侧的两个小回路。实轴上标出了 -1 的位置，并用虚线标出约 -0.8 和 -0.4 的位置；两个小回路大致位于 -0.8 到 0 附近。曲线箭头显示大的外回路按顺时针方向绕行；左侧小回路也按顺时针方向绕行；右侧小回路不包围 -0.5 点。

推理：闭环特征方程为 1 + K G(s) = 0，因此在 G(s) 的 Nyquist 图上应考察临界点 -1/K。已知 K = 2，所以临界点为 -1/2 = -0.5。由图中尺度看，-0.5 位于 -0.8 与 -0.4 之间。该点被大的外回路包围一次，也被左侧小回路包围一次，而未被右侧小回路包围。根据箭头，这两个相关包围均为顺时针包围，因此净顺时针包围数为 2。题中给出 G(s) 在闭右半平面无极点，所以 P = 0。Nyquist 判据下，闭环在闭右半平面的极点数等于该净顺时针包围数，即 2。

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Consider a closed-loop control system with unity negative feedback and \(KG(s)\) in the forward path, where the gain \(K = 2\). The complete Nyquist plot of the transfer function \(G(s)\) is shown in the figure. Note that the Nyquist contour has been chosen to have the clockwise sense. Assume \(G(s)\) has no poles on the closed right-half of the complex plane. The number of poles of the closed-loop transfer function in the closed right-half of the complex plane is ______.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, the horizontal axis is labeled Re G(s), and the vertical axis is labeled Im G(s). The Nyquist curve contains a large outer elliptical closed loop, as well as two small loops near the negative real-axis side. The position of -1 is marked on the real axis, and the positions of approximately -0.8 and -0.4 are marked with dashed lines; the two small loops are roughly located near -0.8 to 0. The curve arrows show that the large outer loop travels clockwise; the left small loop also travels clockwise; the right small loop does not enclose the -0.5 point.

Reasoning: The closed-loop characteristic equation is 1 + K G(s) = 0, therefore on the Nyquist plot of G(s), the critical point -1/K should be examined. Given K = 2, the critical point is -1/2 = -0.5. Judging from the scale in the figure, -0.5 is between -0.8 and -0.4. This point is enclosed once by the large outer loop, and also enclosed once by the left small loop, but is not enclosed by the right small loop. According to the arrows, these two relevant encirclements are both clockwise encirclements, therefore the net number of clockwise encirclements is 2. The problem states that G(s) has no poles in the closed right half-plane, so P = 0. Under the Nyquist criterion, the number of closed-loop poles in the closed right half-plane equals this net number of clockwise encirclements, namely 2.
